### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **15** documentable anchor(s).

**11** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via AuthPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx`  _(via AuthPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via AuthPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b4921982a0fd09f763d61adf4d4315698ef493ad` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `415782fc25b040d42da7fec6651650ae450ab98d` — the merge of head `5dd302a33d1a9cc64c206f477814013f09852119` into base `b4921982a0fd09f763d61adf4d4315698ef493ad`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 415782fc25b040d42da7fec6651650ae450ab98d && git checkout 415782fc25b040d42da7fec6651650ae450ab98d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b4921982a0fd09f763d61adf4d4315698ef493ad 5dd302a33d1a9cc64c206f477814013f09852119 && git checkout -B drift-repro b4921982a0fd09f763d61adf4d4315698ef493ad && git merge --no-ff 5dd302a33d1a9cc64c206f477814013f09852119

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b4921982a0fd09f763d61adf4d4315698ef493ad
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b4921982a0fd09f763d61adf4d4315698ef493ad` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `db39eb311eb288d7e0eccb1ae74751c232a9accf`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sign-in-method-floor.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sign-in-method-floor.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/cloud-managed.test.ts + read, not reviewed: .changeset/managed-email-password-held-off.md
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none
Regen-provenance: none

First round on this PR. Inputs: card #34174, triage 7211578688, claim 7222972851, dev report 7224276022 (its conclusions not adopted), the PR body's declaration lines, `git diff origin/main...db39eb31` (merge base `4af32b99`), AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3, `execution-duties.md` lines 104 to 110, the stock changesets and `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/CHANGELOG.md`, and the check-runs on this head. Nothing was built or run. The PR as declared (`Clause-②: no`, no schema or governed path) touches none of the four contract faces; this record exists because the declaration itself is the question, and finding M1 puts the PR on the narrowing face.

### ① Derived judgments

- What the diff changes at a published door (`PUT /api/settings/auth`, `SettingsService.setMany('auth', …)`), on a cloud-managed runtime whose deployment declared `emailAndPassword.enabled: false`:
  - narrowed: a save that changes `email_password_enabled` to a value that reads on answers `400 SETTINGS_VALIDATION` and writes nothing in the batch, where it was stored;
  - widened: a save that turns the key off or clears it is accepted where the sign-in floor refused it with `constraint.lastSignInMethod: email_password` (the PR body's own measurement on main: `SAVE-FALSE err SETTINGS_VALIDATION`; its ablation: with the new branch removed, the clear case is refused);
  - widened, response: the field error at that key can now carry `constraint: { cloudManaged: true, declaredEmailPassword: false }` and the new sentence `managedEmailPassword`;
  - applied state: a stored value that reads on no longer reaches `getPublicConfig().emailPassword.enabled` there.
- `Clause-②: no`: WRONG. The line this diff owes is `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`.
  - The arm. AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3 gives the arm no carve-out for a refusal that depends on host state, and `execution-duties.md` line 107 names "narrowing a published accept set" as the case. The auth settings save is treated as a published accept set by every earlier change to this same predicate: the floor's introduction (`yes (narrowing)`, "a save an administrator could make before is now refused at the settings save door with the existing `SETTINGS_VALIDATION` / `invalid_value` field error"), the refused clear, and `3372da0` (`yes (narrowing)`, the `googleLocalOff` refusal). All three carry a BREAKING banner and an ADR-0087 marker.
  - A refusal conditioned on what the deployment mounts or declares is declared the same way in stock: `.changeset/pre/33933-knowledge-settings-with-service.md` ("on a deployment that does not mount …") and `.changeset/pre/37678-knowledge-turso-settings-group.md`, both `no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `patch`.
  - The value. `3372da0` declared `yes` for the exact parallel of this diff's widened half: "a save of `email_password_enabled: false` answers `200` and saves, where it answered `400 SETTINGS_VALIDATION`, because the sign-in page offers no email and password there either way", plus a new copy key in all eleven locales. `execution-duties.md` line 109: removing a deliberate guard's refusal is `yes` unless the `no` cites the published text that already denies the refusal; this `no` cites none.
  - The sibling managed-door changesets the dev report rests on do not bear on this. `35220`, `34889` (`no`) and `34651`, `34171` (`yes (widening)`) add an action, reword copy or add a response key; none refuses a request that was accepted.
  - The negative boundary (`execution-duties.md` line 105, a runtime security change is not clause ②) speaks to the `yes | no` value, not to the arm: `35184-dev-seed-retire-at-boot` and both `password-reset-*` changesets are security behaviour changes and carry `(narrowing)`.
  - The claim's `Clause-②: no` was a prediction made before the diff existed; `landing-operations.md` line 5 makes the diff the fact.
- `Metadata-protocol: none`: RIGHT. No authorable metadata key, value or type changes; a settings value is runtime state, the reading `33933` records in its ADR-0087 marker.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/plugin-auth` patch: right, and it stays `patch` after M1. Step 3: the level follows the metadata-protocol kind alone, and `none` takes `patch`; a non-protocol narrowing "ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition".
- What the changeset lacks once the arm is declared: the BREAKING banner, exactly one ADR-0087 marker, and the corrected declaration line. `check:adr-0087-registration` reads the arm from the changeset body, so it is green today only because the arm is absent. With `Metadata-protocol: none` the `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` category stays open to it (the #32601 refusal applies to `narrowed` only).
- The changeset body states both halves of the save door accurately. "Nothing to migrate" holds: a row stored on is left in place, not applied, and named in the log with its remedy.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]`. No note owed.
- `Security-touching: yes`: the diff decides whether a sign-in method is advertised and lets one save past the last-sign-in-method guard.
  - The apply-side skip is safe. The condition is `enabled && source !== 'env' && cloudManaged && declared off`; it only ever withholds an `enabled: true` patch, so it cannot turn a method off or admit anyone. An `OS_AUTH_EMAIL_PASSWORD_ENABLED` value still applies as the deployment's own declaration. The other `emailAndPassword` keys in the pass are untouched.
  - It is logged: once at `error` with the remedy, re-armed when the condition clears. The same level the pass uses for a `membership_policy` it ignores.
  - The floor bypass for off and clear is safe on this runtime: the running value is off before and after the save, so the save removes no way in.
- Envelope: matches the write-predicate convention. The predicate returns `SettingsWriteRefusal` (`message`, `constraint`); `refuseByWritePredicates` wraps it as `invalid_value` at the key and throws `SettingsValidationError` for the whole batch before any row is written. No new error code, so `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER` is not touched.
- Admin update-user: the pin asserts `400` and `PASSWORD_CANNOT_BE_UPDATED_VIA_UPDATE_USER` for a member and for an identity-provider user on a managed runtime, the member's hash unchanged and no credential created. That is the right shape for a vendor behaviour the card asked to be checked; no code change is owed.
- SQL push-down: the diff adds no query. Nothing to report.
- Main: merge base is `4af32b99`; PR `mergeable_state` reads `blocked`, not `dirty`.
- Check-runs on this head, read at 2026-11-27T17:22:40Z: 50 runs, 14 success, 16 skipped, 20 in progress, none failed.
  - Success so far: Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Type Check · debt ledger, Test UI, Check PR Size, Plan Test Core shards, Auto Label, Flag docs affected, filter.
  - Not yet answered: Build Core, Test Core 1 to 10, Live E2E UI, Type Check (workspace, source gates, consumer gates), four Lint families.
  - "All green" is not established on this head. No auto-merge is armed.

### ④ Design judgment

Owed on the narrowing face (M1); judged over the whole diff outside the changeset.

- Both halves are needed, and the split is the right one. The settings service asks a predicate only about a change from the resolved value (`refuseByWritePredicates`: `stableStringify(next) === stableStringify(current)` skips), and with nothing stored the key resolves to the manifest default `true`. So a save door alone cannot stop a re-save of the default or reach a row stored earlier; the apply-side skip is the guarantee and the door is the loud answer. This meets the card's Expected in both of its offered forms.
- No tolerant fallback is added: the deployment's declaration is the authority and the stored value is refused or left unapplied, not reinterpreted.
- Off and clear pass: verified in the predicate (`readToggle(next, false)`: `false`, `'false'`, `0`, `null` all return before the floor) and pinned by two cases.
- CONTROLs: self-hosted with the same declaration still applies the stored toggle and the floor still refuses turning it off; managed with email and password declared on is judged by the floor as before. `emailPasswordHeldOffByHost` requires both `cloudManaged() === true` and `declaredEmailPasswordEnabled() === false`, and an absent dep reads as not managed, so no other caller's behaviour moves.
- Locale strings: `managedEmailPassword` is present in all eleven tables (en, zh-CN, ja-JP, es-ES, zh-Hant, ar, fr, pt-BR, ru, de, ko), and `Record<SettingsCopyLocale, SignInFloorCopy>` makes a missing one a type error. Each says the same four things: managed, declared off, cannot be turned on here, nothing saved.

M1 (must-fix): the declaration line is wrong in the PR body and the changeset.
- Both read `Clause-②: no`. The diff refuses a save that was accepted and accepts a save that was refused, at a published door (①).
- Owed: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` with the narrowed and widened halves named, in the PR body and the changeset body; the BREAKING banner and one ADR-0087 marker in the changeset; a `Skills-docs:` line in the PR body; the full dogfood battery pinned to the final head in the dev report (`os-dev.md` line 219); the seat's note against claim 7222972851, whose line reads `Clause-②: no`. Whether the title takes `!` follows the repo's own rule for a BREAKING changeset; the three precedents on this door carry it.
- No code change is asked for by M1.

S1 (should-fix): the Google leg of the floor trusts a batch value the runtime will not apply.
- `signInMethodFloorPredicate`, `emailPasswordAfter`: when the batch carries `email_password_enabled`, the value is read from the batch. On a held-off runtime a batch of `{ email_password_enabled: true, google_enabled: false }` where `true` is no change (the manifest default, or a row already stored on) asks no predicate at the email key, and at the Google key reads email and password as on after the save, so the floor passes. The runtime keeps email and password off, so the save can remove the last way in the page offers.
- Reach is narrow: it needs no identity provider row and no host sign-in handoff, and a managed runtime normally has one. The fix is one condition: `emailPasswordAfter` is false when `emailPasswordHeldOffByHost(deps)`. A case beside the new describe pins it.

Nits, none with an effect on correctness or the contract:
- N1. The door reads an unreadable `next` as off (`readToggle(next, false)`) and the settings pass reads an unreadable stored value as on (`asBoolean(value, true)`). The toggle's declared type refuses such a value before any predicate runs, so nothing reaches the gap.
- N2. A `false` row saved here without the floor's judgment would apply if the deployment were later redeployed with email and password declared on. On a managed runtime the host refuses every password door either way.
- N3. `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx` (line 833) and `self-hosting.mdx` (line 805) state the floor's refusal without the managed case. Goes with the `Skills-docs:` line M1 owes.
- N4. The display gap the dev report files as out of scope (the settings page shows the default `true` while the runtime runs off) is real and is the reason a re-save of the default is reachable from the console. A card, not a condition here.

Must-fix: M1. Should-fix: S1.

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5dd302a33d1a9cc64c206f477814013f09852119`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sign-in-method-floor.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sign-in-method-floor.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/cloud-managed.test.ts + read, not reviewed: .changeset/managed-email-password-held-off.md, content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx, content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

Delta round by the reviewer of record 7224378765 (FAIL at `db39eb31`, M1 and S1 open). Inputs: `git diff db39eb31 5dd302a3` (two commits, five files), the PR's current title and body, dev report 7225675485 (its conclusions not adopted), the seat's claim note 7224397824, and the check-runs on this head. Nothing was built or run. `auth-plugin.ts` and `cloud-managed.test.ts` are byte-identical to the head the first record reviewed; its judgments on them carry unchanged.

### ① Derived judgments

- The delta:
  - `sign-in-method-floor.ts`: one condition. `emailPasswordAfter` is false when `emailPasswordHeldOffByHost(deps)`.
  - `sign-in-method-floor.test.ts`: one new case, and the describe's `SettingsService` takes the file's existing `ConfidentialTestAdapter` so the Google secret can be stored.
  - The changeset: the declaration line, a `Skills-docs:` line, one ADR-0087 marker, the BREAKING banner, a What-to-do line, `!` in the summary.
  - Two docs pages gain a paragraph each on the managed case.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`: RIGHT. The changeset and the PR body both name the narrowed half (the refused save, the stored value not applied, the Google leg) and the widened half (off and clear accepted without the floor, the new constraint shape, the `managedEmailPassword` key in 11 locales). The two texts agree.
- `Metadata-protocol: none`: RIGHT, unchanged.
- The S1 change adds one more narrowed case, and the declaration names it: on a held-off runtime a Google removal is now refused where the batch also carried an unchanged `email_password_enabled: true`.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/plugin-auth` patch: right. The kind is `none`, and a non-protocol narrowing ships `patch` with its banner and disposition.
- The changeset now carries the BREAKING banner, exactly one marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, open to it because the kind is `none`), and both declaration lines. Check Changeset is success on this head (both runs).
- The marker's justification is accurate: no schema key, accepted value or metadata type moves, and stored rows are left in place.
- The PR title carries `!`, as the three earlier changes on this door do.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]`. No note owed.
- The seat's note against claim 7222972851 is on the card (7224397824). The bookkeeping M1 asked for is done.
- `Security-touching: yes`, as before. The delta tightens the floor: it can only add a refusal at a `google_*` key on a held-off runtime, and cannot admit a save the floor refused.
- The dev report pins the dogfood battery to this head: 490 files passed, 3 skipped; 4144 tests passed, 68 skipped; no failures. Read from the report, not re-run here.
- SQL push-down: the delta adds no query. Nothing to report.
- Main: the head merges without conflict (merge-tree, no checkout). Merge base `4af32b99`.
- Check-runs on this head, read at 2026-11-27T18:38:46Z: 59 runs, 42 success, 17 skipped, none failed, none in progress. All green is established on this head. No auto-merge is armed.

### ④ Design judgment

Findings of the first record, at this head:

M1 (must-fix): closed.
- Declaration, banner, marker, `Skills-docs:` line, title, battery and claim note are all in place (①, ②, ③).

S1 (should-fix): closed.
- The condition sits where the first record placed it. The `email_password_enabled` key itself still returns before it on a held-off runtime, so the off and clear path is unchanged; off a held-off runtime the helper is false and the expression reads as before, so both CONTROLs are unaffected.
- The new case is the scenario the finding named: Google in force as the last way in, then `{ email_password_enabled: true, google_enabled: false }` with `true` as no change. It asserts the refusal at `google_enabled` with `lastSignInMethod: google`, that Google stays stored on, and that email and password stays off.

Nits, none with an effect on correctness or the contract:
- N1 (open, accepted). The door and the settings pass read an unreadable value with opposite fallbacks; type validation runs first.
- N2 (open, accepted). A `false` row saved here without the floor would apply after a redeploy that declares email and password on.
- N3: closed. `self-hosting.mdx` and `sso.mdx` state the managed case, and the text matches the code: refused on, stored on not applied, off and clear accepted, the env declaration still applies, the Google leg.
- N4 (open, a card). The settings page shows the default `true` on a declared-off deployment: #38029.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

## 维护者速读
- 托管环境（部署声明不提供邮箱密码登录）里，管理员在设置页把「邮箱/密码登录」打开会被拒绝并给出本地化说明；已存的打开值也不再生效，登录页不会再画出注定 409 的密码表单。
- 同时，在这种环境里关掉或清空这个开关不再被「至少保留一种登录方式」拦住，因为密码登录本来就不可用。
- 自建部署、以及声明提供密码登录的托管环境不变。文档两处已补充托管情况。
- 要你做什么：用 os-zhuang 批准本 PR（收窄类改动需授权批准）。契约审核 PASS 记录 7225728561，Head-sha `5dd302a33d1a9cc64c206f477814013f09852119`。

席位意见：首轮契约审核 FAIL（声明应为收窄 + 一处判定漏洞），返工后全部关闭；CI 全绿；新发现的设置页显示问题已立卡 #38029。建议批准。

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · repo:objectstack#6 · head `5dd302a33d1a9cc64c206f477814013f09852119`

- Shape: draft → main, `Fixes #34174`, title carries `!`.
- Premise measured on main `4af32b99` (dev report 7224276022): a stored `email_password_enabled = true` flipped `getPublicConfig().emailPassword.enabled` to true on a managed, declared-off runtime; the save asked no predicate.
- Declaration change against claim 7222972851: noted at 7224397824; the PR declares `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, patch, BREAKING banner, ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, `Skills-docs: none`.
- Review history: contract review FAIL 7224378765 (M1, S1) → rework → PASS 7225728561, no must-fix or should-fix open.
- Admin update-user: better-auth refuses `data.password` on every deployment; pinned on a managed runtime, no code change.
- Gates: check-runs at head 42 success, 17 skipped, 0 failed (reviewer read 18:38Z); dogfood battery at this head 490 files / 4144 tests passed (dev report 7225675485).
- Follow-ups: #38029 (settings page shows the default on a declared-off deployment). N1, N2 left as nits.
